story: What can I do under the Payment of Wages Act? My company in Hyderabad hasn't paid my October 2026 salary of Rs 30,000.

timeline.user_words: My company in Hyderabad hasn't paid my October 2026 salary of Rs 30,000.

facts.user_goal: What can I do under the Payment of Wages Act?

rules.name: monthly_due_date
rules.message: Wages for October 2026 were due before the end of 07 November 2026 (the 7th of the next month).
rules.label: When wages were due

rules.name: wage_claim_limitation
rules.message: File your wage claim before 07 Nov 2029 (1095 days left). This counts 3 years from 07 Nov 2026 (when October 2026 wages fell due; each later month has its own, later deadline). Don't wait for the last date.
rules.label: Last date to file your wage claim

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 1 month(s) x Rs 30,000 = Rs 30,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

answer.summary: Your October 2026 salary of Rs 30,000 was due before 07 November 2026 and is still unpaid. You can file a claim with the wage authority for your unpaid wages. The employer must prove they paid you. You can also claim compensation if you win. The law that applies now is the Code on Wages, 2019.

claims.text: Your salary of Rs 30,000 for October 2026 was due before 07 November 2026.
Unpaid wages include your basic pay, dearness allowance, and any retaining allowance. HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment.
The employer must prove they paid you the wages.
You can file a claim with the wage authority for your unpaid wages. The authority can order up to ten times the claim as compensation.
The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 was repealed and replaced by the Code on Wages, 2019.

support.text: Your salary of Rs 30,000 for October 2026 was due before 07 November 2026.
support.reason: Section 17(1)(iv) states that for monthly basis employment, wages shall be paid 'before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month.' For October 2026, the seventh day of the succeeding month (November 2026) is 7 November 2026. The sentence says 'before 07 November 2026,' which is consistent with 'before the expiry of the seventh day' (i.e., before 7 November).

support.text: Unpaid wages include your basic pay, dearness allowance, and any retaining allowance. HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states that HRA (house rent allowance) is excluded from wages in section 2(y) - it is listed under 'does not include' as item (b) 'house rent allowance.' It also explicitly excludes overtime allowance in item (h). The sentence incorrectly includes both HRA and overtime as wages.

support.text: The employer must prove they paid you the wages.
support.reason: Section 59 states: 'the burden to prove that the said dues have been paid shall be on the employer.' This directly supports that the employer must prove they paid the wages.

support.text: You can file a claim with the wage authority for your unpaid wages. The authority can order up to ten times the claim as compensation.
support.reason: Section 45(2) states that the authority 'may order, having regard to the circumstances under which the claim arises, the payment of compensation in addition to the claim determined, which may extend to ten times of the claim determined.' This directly supports both the ability to file a claim with the wage authority and the up to ten times compensation.

support.text: The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 was repealed and replaced by the Code on Wages, 2019.
support.reason: Section 69(1) states: 'The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 and the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 are hereby repealed.' This directly supports that the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 was repealed.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for payment of unpaid wages

I was employed with you at a monthly wage of Rs 30,000. My wages for October 2026 have not been paid.

I request you to pay the unpaid amount of Rs 30,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter, to my bank account [FILL: account details].

If the amount is not paid, I intend to file a claim before the authority under the Code on Wages, 2019, which may also award compensation, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
